claim: In JNext a probe, rule or breakpoint at an address that runs with interrupts on can fire twice when an interrupt lands on it; guard against the duplicate and count completed updates only.

evidence.text: A probe at a loop head gave one extra update and read as a run shifted by one; the pace script now ignores a second firing within 20,000 T.
Probe at 0xA385 with interrupts on: an execute rule fires twice when an interrupt lands on it, a false update parts lockstep; guarded in the pace profile.
An execute event can occur both before and after an accepted interrupt at the same CALL.
JNext can report an execute address again after an IRQ; one-shot phase flags and nested-ledger negatives prevent double accounting.
An execute breakpoint can fire twice around an interrupt; do not read an entry duplicate as another effect request.

next_check: In the pace script log the cycle count with each probe hit and warn on a second hit within a few T of the first.
